strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing task.start can admit or replay exactly one next task from a current runtime-recorded continue_development product decision.
Rust validates explicit continuation authorization, source task/run state, current product decision status, next action, and expected SHA-256 fingerprints before task creation.
TaskStarted evidence and task records expose bounded product_continuation_provenance so headless callers can see which product decision admitted the next task.
Continuation creates the next runtime task without running it, preserving explicit caller control over subsequent task.run execution.
Admission and provenance expose only bounded ids, enum-like status/action strings, and SHA-256 fingerprints rather than raw product evidence or ledger content.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent structured ledger, agent_loop, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: Existing task.start can create or replay one bounded product-continuation task from a runtime-recorded continue_development decision after explicit authorization and expected decision/evidence fingerprint checks.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Arbitrary task.start can start any task and headless.run.drive can record a continue decision, but neither binds the next task to the current product decision or makes retries duplicate-free.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless controller would still stitch continue_development decisions to follow-up tasks outside Rust authority, allowing duplicate next tasks or unproven continuation work after restarts.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M51.3.1 decision uniqueness, M52.1 product evidence derivation, and M52.2 generic product policy ownership because this is downstream task admission from an already-recorded decision.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing task.start with product_continuation_source and bounded product_continuation_admission metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust re-reads the source task/run ledger, requires the latest addressed HeadlessRunProductCompletionDecisionRecorded event to be continue_development with next_action plan_next_phase, validates expected fingerprints, creates or replays one task, and records bounded provenance.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A restarted headless caller can resubmit the same admission request and receive the same next task/run instead of reinterpreting raw ledger data or creating a duplicate task.
answers.milestone_progress: This establishes the first M53 continuation primitive needed before later phases can route or drive admitted continuation tasks.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M53.1 updates the current and archived phase manifests for a real product-continuation admission capability. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and this is not a wrapper-only phase.

exit_criteria: Existing task.start accepts product_continuation_source without adding a JSON-RPC method

Admission validates explicit authorization, source task/run, current source decision id, continue_development status, plan_next_phase next action, and expected decision/evidence/completion fingerprints before task creation
A valid request creates one Created task with bounded product_continuation_provenance and TaskStarted evidence
Exact replay returns the same continuation task/run and does not append a duplicate TaskStarted event
Product-complete, blocked-by-product-evidence, stale fingerprint, malformed, missing, unauthorized, and conflicting continuation evidence fail closed before continuation task creation
The admitted task is not automatically run and does not invoke provider, verifier, apply, shell, git, network, service, or workspace mutation paths

RPC and ledger metadata remain bounded and exclude raw prompts, provider responses, final responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, and secrets
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test task_start_admits_product_continuation_and_replays_without_running validates valid admission, bounded provenance/result metadata, no automatic run, exact replay, duplicate-free TaskStarted evidence, and denial for stale fingerprint, missing authorization, product_complete, and blocked_by_product_evidence.

VSIX runtimeClient protocol test validates productContinuationSource request transport, product_continuation_admission result metadata, false authorization rejection, raw-field rejection, and invalid next_action rejection.

accepted_capability: Existing task.start admits or replays one Rust-owned next task from a bounded continue_development product decision under explicit authorization and expected fingerprint checks
safety_boundary: Only current continue_development decisions with next_action plan_next_phase can admit a continuation task
Expected decision, accepted-completion, terminal-completion, completion-closure, and product-evidence fingerprints are required
Exact replay is duplicate-free; conflicting same-decision admission fails closed
Continuation task is Created only and must be run explicitly by existing task.run authority
Ledger and RPC expose only bounded ids, statuses, next action, replay state, and SHA-256 fingerprints
VSIX validates transport shape only; Rust owns product-continuation policy
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No automatic planning, task run, provider call, verification, apply, shell, git, network, service, or workspace mutation
No raw Product Charter, manifest, spec, ledger, prompt, provider, file, command, output, environment, absolute path, canonical path, or secret exposure
No milestone closeout in this implementation PR
rejected_alternatives: Adding a product continuation inspection RPC was rejected because admission behavior must change through existing task.start.
Letting callers start arbitrary follow-up tasks after continue_development was rejected because it leaves the continuation boundary outside Rust authority.
Automatically running the admitted continuation task was rejected because M53.1 only creates the replay-safe next task; execution routing belongs to a later phase.
Storing raw product evidence or ledger payloads in provenance was rejected because continuation metadata must remain bounded and replay-safe.
Broad runtime modularization was deferred so this remains a bounded vertical slice.
technical_debt: crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be split only in a cohesive future refactor.
M53.1 admits the next task but does not yet route explicit continuation execution through headless drive.
The product completion policy schema remains intentionally minimal from M52.
next_capability_rationale: M53.2 should route explicit execution of an admitted product-continuation task through existing run-control with freshness checks rather than adding a report or inspection surface.
